policy_name: LSE Principles and Guidance for AI-assisted Marking & Feedback
issuing_authority: London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) Education Committee (approved by Chair's Action); authored by the Eden Centre
country_region: United Kingdom (London School of Economics and Political Science)
regulatory_regime: Institutional academic policy (education/assessment); refers to UK GDPR
geo_constraints: Marking, feedback and moderation on LSE programmes (taught-programme dissertations excluded in the 2025/26 pilot year)

locale_context.region: Europe › United Kingdom (London School of Economics)
locale_context.regulation: Institutional academic policy · principles plus guidance, pilot year 2025/26
locale_context.culture: UK higher-education self-governance: academic judgement and student trust are central, AI use is neither required nor discouraged but must be transparent, human-led and confined to approved enterprise tools; developed jointly with KCL and Southampton.

key_dates.event: Executive summary notes approval by Education Committee in November 2025

versions.title: Approved by Chair's Action, 7 November 2025
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.
versions.note: Principles apply for a pilot year 2025/26 and are then to be reviewed.

covered_entities: LSE academic staff (markers, second markers, moderators, teaching assistants)
covered_systems: GenAI tools (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
unsupported GenAI tools (only with rationale and consent)
exceptions: dissertations on taught programmes (excluded in the pilot year)
automated marking of objective formats (MCQs, online quizzes) predating GenAI
spell-checking, grammar-checking and proofreading tools (e.g. Grammarly) are not AI-assisted marking
conditions: use of AI is optional; the rules govern how, not whether
objective: Set principles and guidelines for responsible, transparent, human-led use of GenAI in marking, feedback and moderation at LSE, protecting students and trust while allowing safe experimentation.
principles: no AI detection of student AI use
conflict_rule: Standard university regulations apply: where AI-assisted feedback has been appropriately used, challenges to academic judgement will not be accepted (s.3.1); LSE's moderation process is unchanged.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/lse-marking.pdf). The copy is the version 'revised post EC Nov 2025' with an executive summary (PDF dated 2 Dec 2025). Approved by Chair's Action on 7 Nov 2025 for a pilot year 2025/26, after which it is to be reviewed, so a later version may exist. Treated as an enforceable internal policy because its principles use 'must' and prohibit AI-generated marking, though the document also calls itself guidance and is neutral on whether staff use AI at all. No official LSE URL is printed in the document.

clauses.original_text: However, the use AI-generated marking and feedback, where AI systems independently generate marks and/or feedback with minimal or no human involvement is not permitted. The only exception to this prohibition is for automated marking of objective assessment formats such as multiple-choice questions (MCQs), online quizzes, or similar computer-marked assessments where automated marking has been an established practice predating GenAI tools.
clauses.object: AI-generated marking and feedback (minimal or no human involvement)
clauses.requirement: AI may not independently generate marks or feedback
clauses.exception: automated marking of objective formats (MCQs, online quizzes) established before GenAI
clauses.purpose: preserve human academic judgement and student trust
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Grammar ('the use AI-generated') as in source. Reinforced in s.3.1: AI 'cannot replace human academic judgment in determining marks, conducting moderation, or making final assessment decisions'.

clauses.original_text: Staff must clearly communicate to students when and how they use AI tools for marking and feedback
clauses.object: when and how AI tools are used for marking and feedback
clauses.requirement: disclose AI use in marking and feedback to students
clauses.condition: where AI tools are used in marking/feedback
clauses.purpose: transparency; preserve trust between staff and students
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: First principle ('Transparency first' in the executive summary). Bullet has no closing full stop in the source.

clauses.original_text: Staff must use LSE approved GenAI tools - such as Claude AI and Microsoft Copilot - for any AI-assisted activities related to assessment, including feedback, marking, and moderation. These tools are selected to ensure compliance with data protection regulations (e.g. UK GDPR), and offer enterprise-grade assurances around security, data integrity, privacy, and responsible AI use.
clauses.object: LSE-approved GenAI tools (Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.requirement: use only approved enterprise GenAI tools for assessment-related AI use
clauses.exception: s.4.1: if unsupported tools are used, staff should explain their rationale and obtain student and institutional consent
clauses.purpose: data protection, security and privacy of student work
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Section 4.1 softens this to 'should use institutionally approved GenAI tools' and allows unsupported tools with student and institutional consent, so the MUST is qualified.

clauses.original_text: Academic staff should not use GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI, as these tools are unreliable
clauses.object: GenAI tools to detect students' use of GenAI
clauses.requirement: do not use GenAI-based detection of student AI use
clauses.purpose: avoid unreliable detection leading to unfair outcomes
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used as AI-use detectors
clauses.interpretation_notes: Bullet has no closing full stop in the source.

clauses.original_text: Staff must not include student details or upload student work into GenAI tools without explicit permission. This prevents personal data from being collected, stored, accessed, and shared without consent.
clauses.requirement: no student details or work in GenAI tools without explicit permission
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: PDF line break inside 'shared / without consent' rejoined. Scenarios show staff using anonymised summaries instead of uploading student work.

clauses.original_text: Staff must provide human oversight at every stage of their approach. GenAI can generate incorrect responses based on probabilities and biases.
clauses.requirement: human oversight at every stage of AI-assisted marking and feedback
clauses.purpose: catch incorrect or biased AI outputs
clauses.affected_asset: accuracy and fairness of feedback and marks
clauses.applicable_systems: GenAI tools used in marking, feedback and moderation (LSE-approved: Claude AI, Microsoft Copilot)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Companion guideline: 'Staff should ensure AI-assisted feedback does not independently determine marks or academic judgements.'
